{
  "reviewer_task_id": "review-synthesis-web",
  "target_artifact": "/home/grammy-jiang/Projects/msgloom/research/08-multimodal-content-understanding/runs/6efd3430f24f/analysis/synthesis.json",
  "status": "rejected",
  "issues": [
    "Finding 7 overstates the reduced evidence. The cited analyses support gains from textual-reference/coreference modeling for pronouns (doi-10-18653-v1-2025-acl-long-547), spatial/scene-graph features for multimodal coreference (manual-bc798b0eed), and low-level UI referring/grounding supervision (2404.05719). J-CRe3 (manual-d896e242a6) establishes that omitted/zero references occur and can be annotated, but its supplied findings do not show that explicit supervision improves grounding of omitted references. The Scene-Text REC analysis (doi-10-1109-tmm-2022-3219642) establishes the task and mechanism but the reduced findings supplied here do not report a controlled improvement attributable specifically to scene-text supervision.",
    "Contradiction 1 is framed too specifically as 'Whether explicit grounding supervision improves answer accuracy.' RefChartQA directly tests grounding instruction tuning and shows model-dependent answer gains and losses, but CiteVQA's oracle experiment supplies correct evidence rather than adding grounding supervision, and LAT jointly changes training/reasoning/attribution rather than providing a clean controlled test of grounding supervision alone. The cited results support a broader tension about grounding-oriented training or access to correct evidence, not the stated controlled contradiction.",
    "Contradiction 2 is mislabeled as 'OCR/text pipelines versus native multimodal processing.' MMLongBench-Doc directly compares LVLMs with OCR-fed LLMs, but MMDocRAG's cited result concerns VLM-generated visual descriptions versus OCR-only evidence, and LongDocURL compares structure-preserving parsing with plain PyMuPDF text. Those latter results establish benefits from visually enriched or structure-preserving representations, not necessarily native end-to-end multimodal processing.",
    "Contradiction 5 does not identify a genuine opposing result from CiteVQA. MP-DocVQA and RefChartQA report multiple defensible evidence locations, while CiteVQA explicitly includes a multi-document multiple-gold setting. Scoring against a defined gold evidence set is not evidence that one location is uniquely correct. The valid synthesis point is that single-positive annotations can underrepresent alternative valid evidence, but CiteVQA should not be presented as the contradictory side of that claim.",
    "The version-aware provenance discussion underuses 2609.08364 (SentryLine), which is directly relevant to evolving documents: it represents source document, page, passage text, citation key, and update status and only reports temporal drift when retrieved passages explicitly document a change. This study does not close the cross-version region/cell-lineage gaps, but it materially narrows the claim about what version-aware hierarchical provenance has already been demonstrated and should appear in the relevant theme or gap-status evidence."
  ],
  "unsupported_claims": [
    "Finding 7: the clause implying that explicit grounding/reference supervision has been empirically shown to improve grounding of omitted references is not supported by the supplied key findings. The corpus shows omitted/zero references are represented in J-CRe3 and that textual-reference modeling improves pronoun grounding, but it does not report the claimed omitted-reference improvement.",
    "Contradiction 5: treating CiteVQA as evidence on the opposing side of 'whether one evidence location is uniquely correct' is unsupported by the supplied analysis because CiteVQA itself evaluates multiple-gold evidence settings.",
    "Contradiction 2: characterizing all cited positive alternatives to OCR/plain text as evidence for 'native multimodal processing' goes beyond the supplied analyses; two cited studies instead support visually enriched textual descriptions or structure-preserving parsing."
  ],
  "required_fixes": [
    "Rewrite Finding 7 so that empirically demonstrated improvements are separated from task or dataset coverage. A faithful formulation would say that adjacent-domain studies show improvements from explicit textual-reference/coreference structure, spatial scene structure, and UI referring/grounding supervision, while J-CRe3 separately demonstrates that omitted/zero references and region targets can be represented and evaluated. Do not claim improved omitted-reference grounding unless a supplied analysis reports that result.",
    "Rename and rewrite Contradiction 1 to distinguish three different interventions: grounding instruction tuning in RefChartQA, joint reasoning-and-attribution training in LAT, and oracle provision of correct evidence in CiteVQA. The defensible conclusion is that grounding-oriented interventions or access to correct evidence can help answering in some settings but effects are not universally positive; do not present all three as controlled tests of explicit grounding supervision.",
    "Rename Contradiction 2 to something such as 'Lossy OCR/plain-text representations versus structure- or visually enriched representations.' Preserve the direct MMLongBench-Doc OCR-versus-LVLM result, but describe MMDocRAG and LongDocURL according to what they actually test.",
    "Remove or reformulate Contradiction 5. CiteVQA should not be used as the opposing side because its multiple-gold setting is compatible with the observation that evidence need not be unique. The supported cross-paper synthesis is that MP-DocVQA and RefChartQA expose ambiguity in single-positive localization, while CiteVQA demonstrates one way to accommodate multiple gold evidence items.",
    "Integrate 2609.08364 into the version-aware provenance summary and the relevant open-gap discussion. State that evolving-document QA with document/page/passage/update-status provenance and explicitly evidenced temporal drift has been demonstrated, while exact cross-version region/cell correspondence and old-to-new element lineage remain open."
  ],
  "confidence": 0.97,
  "scores": {
    "faithfulness": 0.88,
    "coherence": 0.79,
    "gap_completeness": 0.93,
    "citation_integrity": true
  },
  "notes": "All cited paper_ids inspected in the synthesis are members of the permitted identifier set, so identifier-level citation integrity passes. Most major findings and all eight open gaps are well supported, and the central conclusion that a complete cross-version workplace-attachment provenance stack remains unvalidated is faithful to the supplied analyses. Rejection is driven by one substantive overreach in Finding 7 and several contradiction entries that conflate different experimental interventions or present compatible evidence as contradictory. These are correctable synthesis-level issues rather than failures of the underlying corpus."
}
